subject: OrbitAI - Orbit11b elevated 5xx pattern and mitigation timeline
messages:
From: Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.ai>
To: Mina Haddad <mina.haddad@redwood.ai>, Sean Gallagher <sean.gallagher@redwood.ai>
Cc: Stephanie Nguyen <stephanie.nguyen@redwood.ai>
Date: 2028-11-22T09:03:00-08:00
Subject: Orbit11b - elevated 5xxs started 09:00 PST

Quick heads up — automated SLO alerts started firing at ~09:00 PST for Orbit11b serving on us-west-2. We're seeing a sustained increase in 5xx responses (primarily 503 and 504) for generation requests with long contexts (>6k tokens).

Initial triage notes:
- Error surface: 70% 503 gateway responses, 25% 504 timeout, 5% model runtime exceptions.
- Affected pools: orbit11b-xlarge-01 through -04 (dedicated clusters for some customers).
- Memory pressure correlates with token-length distribution; KV-cache growth observed.
- Mitigation attempted: increased per-instance request timeout and rolled temporary eviction policy for huge prefixes.

Attachments: ops_log_20281122.txt (selected traces), timeline_capture_20281122.csv (metric series).

I'm escalating since this touches OrbitAI (they're on dedicated capacity on these pools). Will follow up with a customer-facing note once we have mitigation ETA.

—Rishi
Senior SRE, Serving Runtime
Redwood Inference
From: Mina Haddad <mina.haddad@redwood.ai>
To: Jared Cohen <jared.cohen@orbitai.com>
Cc: support@orbitai.com, Sean Gallagher <sean.gallagher@redwood.ai>, Stephanie Nguyen <stephanie.nguyen@redwood.ai>
Date: 2028-11-22T09:40:00-08:00
Subject: Orbit11b elevated 5xx pattern — immediate mitigation and ETA

Jared —

Thanks for the quick sync just now. Short summary for your team: starting at ~09:00 PST we observed an elevated rate of 5xx responses on the Orbit11b serving pool attached to OrbitAI. Our initial analysis shows the failures correlate with very long-context requests that create high KV-cache pressure on the instances and result in request stalls or resource contention.

What we're doing now (immediate):
- Throttling requests above 6k tokens for your dedicated pool (automatic 429s for extreme contexts) to prevent cascading failures.
- Rolling a targeted restart of the four affected instances in a staggered fashion to restore healthy capacity (in progress).
- Applying a short-term kernel config tweak that reduces background GC latency risk.

Estimated timeline: we expect instance roll restarts + config tweak to reduce 5xx rate to baseline within 45–90 minutes. If that doesn't land, next step is an instance reprovision to a larger memory profile (we've pre-approved capacity).

We're tracking this as JIRA-INC-47291 and will share a short postmortem within 48 hours with root cause and remediation.

Attachments: ops_log_20281122.txt (sanitized trace examples).

Apologies for the disruption — we'll keep you updated live in this thread.

Best,
Mina Haddad
Director, Customer Reliability
Redwood Inference
From: Jared Cohen <jared.cohen@orbitai.com>
To: Mina Haddad <mina.haddad@redwood.ai>
Cc: support@orbitai.com
Date: 2028-11-22T10:05:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Orbit11b elevated 5xx pattern — immediate mitigation and ETA

Thanks Mina — appreciate the quick action. Two quick asks from our side: 1) can you confirm whether the throttling is being applied only to our dedicated pool or across shared customers, and 2) what is the rollback mechanism if the kernel tweak increases latency for other workloads?

We rely on long-context calls for a few of our flows; if the throttle will block those we need a short-term workaround or a manual bypass for a small set of IPs.

—Jared
Head of Platform Engineering, OrbitAI
From: Stephanie Nguyen <stephanie.nguyen@redwood.ai>
To: Mina Haddad <mina.haddad@redwood.ai>, Sean Gallagher <sean.gallagher@redwood.ai>
Cc: Jared Cohen <jared.cohen@orbitai.com>, support@orbitai.com
Date: 2028-11-23T14:15:00-08:00
Subject: RE: Orbit11b elevated 5xx pattern — immediate mitigation and ETA

Update: staged restarts completed at 13:20 PST; the 5xx rate dropped from ~18% to ~2.4% by 13:55 PST. We applied the kernel config rollback window and observed improved GC latencies in perf counters.

Action items taken:
- Applied throttling rule scoped to OrbitAI dedicated pool only (no cross-customer impact).
- Opened a short bypass path for three OrbitAI service IPs after manual verification (bypass will be removed after full stability verification).
- Captured heap snapshots and a minimal repro for the model with long prefix sequences (attached heapdump_stub.tgz).

We recommend:
1) Schedule a workload review with OrbitAI to evaluate dataset prep and prefix trimming (help reduce KV growth).
2) Plan a capacity migration to the larger instance profile we discussed if you expect sustained long-context usage.

I'll coordinate a formal postmortem and proposed remediation timeline; targeting a full write-up tomorrow EOD.

Attachments: heapdump_stub.tgz, timeline_capture_20281122.csv.

—Stephanie
SRE, Runtime Reliability
Redwood Inference
From: Mina Haddad <mina.haddad@redwood.ai>
To: Jared Cohen <jared.cohen@orbitai.com>, support@orbitai.com
Cc: Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.ai>, Sean Gallagher <sean.gallagher@redwood.ai>, Stephanie Nguyen <stephanie.nguyen@redwood.ai>
Date: 2028-11-24T16:47:00-08:00
Subject: Orbit11b incident summary, RCA and next steps (JIRA-INC-47291)

Jared / OrbitAI team —

Thanks again for your patience while we triaged the elevated 5xx rate on your Orbit11b dedicated pool. Below is a concise incident summary and planned remediation. We have also attached the sanitized operational logs and timeline.

Summary:
- Incident window: 2028-11-22 09:00 PST — 2028-11-22 14:00 PST (peak failure window).
- Impact: elevated 5xxs (503/504), primarily for generation requests with context >6k tokens; average latency spiked and a subset of requests aborted.
- Root cause: unanticipated growth in KV-cache population for long-context requests interacting with an internal eviction policy bug. The bug caused delayed reclaiming of per-request working sets under certain sequence patterns, leading to transient memory pressure and request stalls.

What we did:
- Scoped throttling to your dedicated pool for contexts >6k tokens.
- Performed staggered instance restarts and applied a short-term kernel tuning to reduce GC-induced stalls.
- Implemented a hotfix to the eviction policy that prevents delayed reclaiming in the identified sequence pattern. Hotfix rolled to production on 2028-11-23 11:00 PST.

Status: hotfix verified across the affected pools; 5xx rate returned to baseline (<0.5%) in monitored windows after the fix. We will leave throttling in monitor-only mode for 72 hours and coordinate removal with you once we confirm stability.

Next steps (timeline):
- 72-hour stability monitor (Nov 24–27).
- Capacity migration plan for OrbitAI (if you expect sustained >6k token usage): engineering proposal by Nov 29.
- Postmortem doc (drive link) expanded with sanitized traces and suggested SDK best-practices for long contexts: https://drive.google.com/open?id=postmortem-orbit11b-20281122

Credits / SLO considerations:
- Given impact to request success rate in the incident window, we will apply a usage credit equivalent to 5% of affected request billable units for the week of Nov 18–24. Our finance and billing team will follow up with a formal credit note and updated invoice lines.

If you'd like, we can set up a technical session next week to walk through the fix and recommended changes to request shaping. Please let me know preferred times.

Apologies again for the disruption and thank you for working with us to get this resolved quickly.

Best regards,
Mina Haddad
Director, Customer Reliability
Redwood Inference

Attachments: ops_log_20281122.txt, timeline_capture_20281122.csv
